raw_text:
Alright, buckle up, buttercups. Wednesday news dump is here, and it's a wild one. Grab your crypto wallet and a strong espresso; we've got billionaires being made by AI doom, geopolitics getting *very* cozy, and a whole lot of packages moving.

Here's the rundown:

Money Talk
- **AI Doom-Scroller cashes in on Anthropic IPO.**
  The irony is rich: An Estonian tech billionaire, infamous for predicting AI's potential to end humanity, is now set to make billions from Anthropic's upcoming IPO. Turns out, even the prophets of AI doom can get *very* rich off the tech they warn about. [S1][S7]
- **Nvidia defies gravity (and Jensen Huang).**
  The AI chip giant just crushed another quarter with strong guidance, despite the recent drama with its former CEO. Interim CEO Colette Kress is talking demand and buybacks, proving that even without its "sugar daddy" Jensen Huang, the AI revolution rolls on. [S4][S48][S53]
- **UK households brace for a painful winter as inflation bites.**
  Typical energy bills are set to jump a brutal 26% — an extra £443 a year starting January — as UK inflation hits a one-year high. Looks like the cost of living crisis is far from over, unless you've been shorting cat food. [S9][S10]
- **Lowe's crushes online, raises outlook.**
  Amidst a sluggish housing market, Lowe's surprised everyone by posting strong online sales, leading them to raise their full-year guidance. Turns out, even when people aren't buying new houses, they still need stuff for the ones they're in. Good for them, bad for the "housing is dead" crowd. [S3]
- **Jeffries takes the speaker gavel (almost).**
  Hakeem Jeffries officially clinched the Democratic nomination for House speaker, a historic step towards becoming the first Black House speaker in January. A little political stability might be just what the markets ordered. [S2][S17][S19][S35]

World Lore
- **Trump plays diplomat: China, Russia, and him walk into a summit.**
  President Trump is having a historic three-way meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in China, with Xi even breaking protocol to greet him on the tarmac. The stated goal is a push to end the Ukraine war, which sounds suspiciously like a sequel to "America First" that nobody asked for. [S16][S20][S23][S24]
- **Israel kicks off new ground op in Gaza.**
  The Israeli military has launched fresh ground operations in central Gaza, targeting Hamas infrastructure. This escalation comes amidst a dire humanitarian situation, reminding us that some conflicts just keep getting grimmer. [S32]
- **ICJ preps for landmark Myanmar genocide verdict.**
  The International Court of Justice is about to drop a major ruling on the Rohingya genocide case. This decision could set significant precedents, especially for the court's upcoming judgment on Israel. Big implications for international justice, or just another paper tiger? We'll see. [S26]
- **Ukraine might trade land for NATO protection.**
  The U.S. is apparently floating the idea of Ukraine ceding parts of Donetsk in exchange for NATO membership or protection. Experts are calling it risky, and you know what? They're probably right. This isn't exactly a simple real estate deal. [S31]

Tech Tea
- **Nvidia hit with ransomware, because why not.**
  Just when you thought the drama around Nvidia's former CEO and market dominance couldn't get more complex, the company apparently got hit with a ransomware attack. Seems like everyone wants a piece of the AI pie, even the hackers. [S36]
- **AI answers are as consistent as a toddler's mood swings.**
  Turns out, if you ask an AI the same 210 buying questions two days in a row, 84% of the answers will change. This is less "intelligence" and more "digital amnesia." Maybe don't trust it with your investment portfolio just yet. [S37]
- **Google Search's AI gets an incognito mode.**
  Google is rolling out temporary threads for its AI Mode in Search, allowing users to converse without their queries polluting search history or future recommendations. Because sometimes, even your AI interactions need a little privacy, especially when you're asking it embarrassing questions. [S41]
- **Banks telling customers: "You're on your own with AI agents."**
  Citi is the latest financial institution to warn customers that if they use personal finance AI agents and get hacked, they might be out of luck. It's a bold strategy, Cotton, to tell your customers that the future of finance is a wild west where they carry all the risk. [S42]
- **OpenAI helps design chips, because of course it does.**
  OpenAI is using its models to advance chip design, which is basically AI making the tools for more AI. It's an ouroboros of silicon, and probably means even faster chips for your next crypto mining rig. [S38]

Creator Szn
- **Creator marketing is eating the ad world alive.**
  The global influencer market is exploding, growing at double the pace of traditional advertising, largely driven by brands funding creators to produce their ads. Traditional agencies, your lunch is officially being eaten by someone with a ring light and a TikTok account. [S56]
- **YouTube creators are turning old videos into new money.**
  Creators are finally realizing their massive back catalogs on YouTube are goldmines for syndication. It's like finding a vintage Supreme drop in your attic, but instead of clothes, it's viral cat videos. [S59]
- **The hunt for transparent CTV ad buying continues.**
  Everyone in the Connected TV (CTV) advertising industry is demanding a clearer "bidstream," but who's actually going to deliver it? It's a transparency problem wrapped in an opaque black box, and advertisers are getting antsy. [S58]

Supply Lines
- **UPS snags Smartways Logistics to boost APAC healthcare.**
  UPS is acquiring Smartways Logistics, a move that significantly expands its specialized healthcare operations in Australia and New Zealand. This is a smart play to capture more high-value, temperature-sensitive cargo in a growing market, showing that package delivery isn't just about brown boxes anymore.
- **DHL Forwarding launches dedicated freighter service for India.**
  DHL Forwarding just rolled out its first-ever dedicated 747 freighter service for India, offering guaranteed cargo space in and out of the country. With India's economy booming, this boosts capacity and reliability for critical trade lanes, a big win for shippers trying to navigate peak season congestion.
- **FedEx opens new Guangzhou international cargo terminal.**
  FedEx has officially launched its International Cargo Terminal 4 at Guangzhou Baiyun Airport, a massive expansion that solidifies its footprint in a key Asian logistics hub. More capacity in Asia means faster transit times and better connections for global supply chains.
- **Amazon brings drone delivery to Hampton Roads next year.**
  Amazon is set to roll out drone delivery services in parts of Hampton Roads, Virginia, starting next year. While still localized, this pushes the envelope on last-mile delivery tech, showing Amazon's relentless pursuit of faster, more automated fulfillment.
- **Transatlantic airfreight rates hit a four-year high.**
  Airfreight rates between Europe and the U.S. have spiked to their highest level since December 2022, jumping 12% last week alone. This surge is due to peak-season demand and tightening capacity, making air cargo a pricey proposition right now, regardless of the FAA ground stop.
- **EU parcel charges are taking a bite out of retail margins.**
  New EU customs duties and handling fees for low-value e-commerce goods are causing headaches for UK retailers, with some Black Friday bundles now facing up to €15 in charges. Expect fewer impulse buys and more calculated shopping across the channel as these costs add up.

Speed Round
- Hakeem Jeffries is about to make history, becoming the first Black House speaker.
- Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is *not* getting reinstated, despite industry pleas.
- Jim Beam is halting production at its flagship distillery as value spirits struggle.
- Google is forcing Android developers to properly support foldable phones by April 2027.
- Black Friday deals are already dropping, with Apple's MacBook Neo getting its largest discount ever.
- Global Muslims expected to outnumber Christians by 2035, driven by fertility rates.
- A Muslim author is suing xAI after Grok was used to digitally strip her hijab.
